meanings.meaning: A priest is someone who offers sacrifices to God and stands between the people and Him. In Israel, the job was given to Aaron's family, from the tribe of Levi.
A priest in other religions is a person who offers sacrifices and does sacred acts for a false god. He acts as a go-between for people and the god they worship, such as Dagon.
The Holy Spirit is God Himself, the third Person of the Trinity, who is one with the Father and the Son. He helps, teaches, strengthens and comforts God's people.
A being without a body, such as an angel or a demon. Good spirits serve God, and bad or unclean spirits are evil.
The part of a person that is not the body, the inner life or soul. It can also mean a person's feeling or attitude, like a spirit of grace.
A covenant is a solemn agreement between two sides. When God makes one, He gives His serious promise and also tells people what they must do to keep it.
A covenant between people is a serious agreement, often made before God as witness. Both sides promise to do something, and the promise must be kept.
A day of rest from work, usually the seventh day of the week. God set it apart as holy, and He gave it to Israel as part of His laws.
A whole year of rest, kept every seventh year by the Israelites. In this year the land was to rest, as a time set apart for the LORD.
A psalmist is someone who writes songs about God or faith. The name is used especially for David and the other writers of the psalms in the Bible.
To scatter a liquid or fine bits of something, like blood, oil, water, or dust, so it falls in small drops or pieces. It can also mean to cleanse or make pure.
To perish is to die or be destroyed. It can also mean to be lost, to pass away, or to come to nothing.
Having all power, with no limit to His strength. Almighty is a name for God, the all-powerful One.
A special piece of priest's clothing with a front and back part, joined at the shoulders and fastened at the waist. The high priest's was embroidered in bright colors.
Something like the priest's ephod that was made and kept for worship, such as in a shrine. Schaff's says other people besides priests also wore an ephod or something like it.
A lump of old dough mixed into fresh dough to make bread rise and turn light. God's people could not use it during Passover or in offerings burned to Him.
A picture of something that spreads secretly through a whole group. It can mean bad teaching or evil, like the Pharisees', or how God's kingdom quietly grows.
Impurity is being unclean or dirty. It can mean being unclean in a religious way, or it can mean anything bad or mixed in that spoils something.
Sorcery is magic that people claimed to do with the help of evil spirits, like telling the future or healing sickness. The Bible warns of very serious punishment for it.
Onyx is a valuable stone with bands of different colors. Its gems were set in the high priest's special clothing, and it came from a land called Havilah.
Offering something to God as an act of worship, such as an animal laid on an altar. People sacrificed to say thank you, to ask for His favor, or to make up for sin.
A blasphemer is a person who speaks about God in a disrespectful, wicked way. In Leviticus, the word is linked to a man who cursed.
A firebrand is a piece of wood that is burning, like a torch or a stick with a glowing end. In the Bible it can also mean a burning arrow or dart.
Stewardship is the office of a steward, which means the position or job a steward holds. In these verses, it is a job connected to God's grace, a mystery, and His work.
Someone from the family line of Ahoah. The name was used for some of David's warriors, like Eleazar, because they were descendants of Ahoah.
Ethanim was the seventh month of the old Hebrew calendar, around September and October. Its name means "month of gifts," and it began the everyday year.
